facts.text: An ultrasonic sensor emits a short burst of inaudibly high-frequency sound and measures the echo to determine the distance to the nearest object within a few meters.
facts.quote: An ultrasonic sensor sends out a short burst of sound too high for people to hear and measures the echo to find the distance to the nearest object within a few meters.

facts.text: Ultrasonic sensors are short-range and coarse in direction because sound is slow and spreads out.
facts.quote: Because sound is slow and spreads out, ultrasonic sensors are short-range and coarse in direction.

facts.text: Ultrasonic sensor range drifts with temperature unless compensated because the speed of sound changes with temperature.
facts.quote: The speed of sound changes with temperature, so range drifts unless compensated.

facts.text: An ultrasonic transducer continues ringing after transmission, creating a dead zone close to the sensor.
facts.quote: The transducer keeps ringing after it transmits, creating a dead zone close to the sensor.

facts.text: Neighboring ultrasonic sensors can hear each other's echoes.
facts.quote: Neighboring sensors hear each other's echoes.

facts.text: Soft, rough or angled surfaces scatter sound away from ultrasonic sensors.
facts.quote: Soft, rough or angled surfaces scatter sound away.

facts.text: Weak points in ultrasonic sensor simulation include diffuse scattering from crushed rock or soil, contamination on the sensor face, water films, wind and temperature gradients, and vibration coupling into the housing.
facts.quote: the simulation weak points as diffuse scattering from crushed rock or soil, contamination on the sensor face, water films, wind and temperature gradients, and vibration coupling into the housing

facts.text: The booklet found no published comparison of ultrasonic sensor simulation with reality in rain, snow, wind, dust or mud.
facts.quote: found no published comparison of simulation with reality in rain, snow, wind, dust or mud

facts.text: The only ultrasonic sensor model validation found by the booklet was industry-authored and concerned a road sensor.
facts.quote: the only model validation found was industry-authored, on a road sensor [Chapter 6]

facts.text: Bench stimulation of real ultrasonic sensors exists only for automotive parking.
facts.quote: Bench stimulation of real ultrasonic sensors exists only for automotive parking [Chapter 7].

facts.text: ISO 16001, the international standard for object detection on earth-moving machines, has annexes for ultrasonic sensors and transponders.
facts.quote: ISO 16001, the international standard for object detection on earth-moving machines, has annexes for ultrasonic sensors and transponders [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Ultrasonic sensors are cheap and cover the very close zone behind a machine where a person on foot is most at risk.
facts.quote: Ultrasonic sensors are cheap and cover the very close zone behind a machine where a person on foot is most at risk

facts.text: The booklet rates ultrasonic sensor simulation evidence as the weakest of all sensor types, so any role for ultrasonic sensors in the program must rest on physical tests.
facts.quote: the booklet rates their simulation evidence the weakest of all sensor types, so any role for them must rest on physical tests [Chapters 6, 9].
